agent_explanations_oldest_first.text: The pairing bug is now clear. In the chat format the solution begins at `pl-1`, with "She" (no leading space), while in the raw format it begins at `pl-2`, with " She" after "Answer:". The first token differs and the offsets don't match. Both texts end with identical tokens, so I'll align from the end. I'll pair position t0 = L0 − r with t3 = L3 − r and keep only positions where both the input token and the target token match. As a check, the layer-0 difference must then be zero. With that I'll recompute the per-layer digit-specific v0 − v3 difference.

With the corrected pairing, the layer-0 difference is exactly zero, so the alignment is right. The v0 − v3 difference is almost the same at digit and non-digit positions (cos 0.8-0.97). It appears at hidden 12, the known layer-11 eval-context offset, and the digit-specific part stays small (0.03 or less of the residual norm) until the last layers (0.066 at the output). So there is no strong digit-specific signal written by one layer, on average. The digit degradation may instead come from a math-triggered component rather than a format-triggered one, so the right contrast is math versus non-math content. Before spending a pass I'll check what fwd_2 (80 texts, all layers' MLP activations) and tf1_groups contain. I believe they were a math/non-math contrast, which would let me look for strongly math-gated "switch" neurons across all 26 layers.

fwd_2 was the earlier math/non-math contrast: 80 short chat prompts in groups A-D, analyzed in blocks 8-17. It produced the layer-10/11 candidates I already tested and closed, so repeating it won't help. A more diagnostic question is what kind of wrong digit the model prefers. Natural confusion would give errors spread across digits or near-miss values. A planted corruption would often show a systematic signature, such as target ±1 or a fixed shift. I'll tabulate (wrong top-1 digit − target digit) mod 10 at digit positions in v0 and v3, separately for all digits and for the first digit after "=". A shift distribution peaked differently in v0 than in v3 would point to a deliberate mechanism. Similar, diffuse distributions would argue the digit gap is generic.

Wrong first digits after "=" are about twice as frequent in the eval format (47 of 933 against 22 of 933). In both formats the errors are mostly ±1 or spread across other digits. So there is no planted fixed shift, rather a general loss of digit confidence in the chat/eval context. I'll look for that loss in the digit readout. At each saved layer, for digit-predicting positions, I'll project the normalized hidden state onto the embedding direction of the correct digit, relative to the mean digit embedding. This is a fixed-vector projection, not a simulation of the model's final layers. I'll compare v0 with v3 to find the layer where v0's correct-digit signal falls behind. A sharp drop at specific layers would localize a component that suppresses or blurs arithmetic in the eval context. A gap that builds gradually would suggest diffuse degradation from the context signal.
